advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure an unresolvable declared base cannot re-seed an execution when base_resolver is None (validate the declared base unconditionally, or seed only after the base is confirmed).
evidence: services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py:362: `if (base and ctx.base_resolver is not None and not await ctx.base_resolver.resolve_base(...))`

services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py:360: comment: `Resolved before the ledger effect because a raised effect leaves its key _PENDING, so validating inside _launch would re-seed an execution and snapshot on every pass.`

`reconcile_intake(..., base_resolver: IntakeBaseResolver | None = None)` — resolver defaults to None, so a library caller with a base: label but no resolver hits the raise-inside-_launch path the comment warns against

services/coordination/idempotency.py:108-113: `run_once` only short-circuits on _COMPLETED; a raised effect never records, so the _PENDING row is re-run (on_conflict_do_nothing) and _launch re-seeds next pass
advisory.finding: When a declared base is supplied but `ctx.base_resolver is None`, the pre-check at _start is skipped and the unresolvable branch is only caught by the raise inside `_launch`, which fires AFTER `execution_seeder.seed()` and snapshot capture have run — orphaning a seeded execution/snapshot and leaving a _PENDING ledger row that re-seeds on the next pass. This is the exact hazard the code comment says the pre-resolve avoids, but the guard makes the pre-resolve conditional on a resolver being wired.
scenarios: A caller of reconcile_intake that passes a ticket carrying a base: label but does not wire base_resolver
A base branch that is deleted from the remote after the resolver was omitted

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid the duplicate git ls-remote for a declared base (reuse the resolved SHA from the pre-check instead of re-resolving inside start).
evidence: services/orchestration/intake_runtime.py:56-57: `start` calls `remote_head(source_location, base)` again for the same repo/branch
services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py:365: pre-check uses `not await ctx.base_resolver.resolve_base(...)` — return value (the SHA) is only tested for truthiness, then discarded
advisory.finding: A declared, resolvable base branch triggers two separate `git ls-remote` subprocess calls per start: once in `_start` via `ctx.base_resolver.resolve_base`, and again inside `TemporalStarter.start` via `remote_head`. The result of the first lookup is discarded (only its truthiness is used), so the SHA is fetched twice.
scenarios: Every intake pass that starts a workflow for a ticket carrying a valid base: label

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a multi-pass test driving the raise-inside-_launch path (_UnresolvableBaseStarter with base_resolver=None) that asserts seeder.seeded and store.by_execution do not grow across passes.
evidence: intake_reconciler.py:360-361: '# Resolved before the ledger effect because a raised effect leaves its key _PENDING, # so validating inside _launch would re-seed an execution and snapshot on every pass.'
intake_reconciler.py:423-427: 'try: outcome = await ctx.ledger.run_once(ref, _launch) except UnresolvableBaseBranch as exc: await _hold(...)'

test_unresolvable_declared_base_holds_once_per_pass_without_growth passes base_resolver=_BaseResolver({}) (pre-check path), never a raising _UnresolvableBaseStarter with base_resolver=None across passes

ABSENCE: no test in test_intake_reconciler.py drives _UnresolvableBaseStarter over multiple _run passes and asserts seeder.seeded / store.by_execution do not grow — the exact regression the comment guards
advisory.finding: The UnresolvableBaseBranch raise-inside-_launch fallback path (used when ctx.base_resolver is None, caught at intake_reconciler.py:423-427) has no multi-pass regression test asserting it does not re-seed an execution/snapshot on subsequent passes. The design comment at lines 360-361 explicitly warns this path leaves the ledger key _PENDING and re-seeds every pass; the only no-growth test (test_unresolvable_declared_base_holds_once_per_pass_without_growth) drives the _BaseResolver pre-check path with base_resolver set, never the raise path.
scenarios: A ticket declares base:gone in an intake context where base_resolver is None, so the branch is only rejected via UnresolvableBaseBranch raised from _launch after the execution has been seeded; on the next pass the still-_PENDING ledger key re-seeds again.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that runs reconcile_intake multiple passes with starter=_UnresolvableBaseStarter('gone') and base_resolver=None over a shared ledger/seeder/store, asserting seeder.seeded and store.by_execution stay bounded (and the hold is recorded each pass or once as the contract requires).
